title: glow's notty stylesheet has no bold, so REDIRECTED help output keeps its ** markers -- not a Utilz defect, and invisible at a terminal
body:
The help renderer processes inline code spans and passes `**` through literally, so every bold span in every help file prints its asterisks to the user.

MEASURED 2026-09-09 by cc, while amending help/prez.md for ST0017/WP-05 (AC-5.2). The defect is PRE-EXISTING and estate-wide; the amendment neither caused it nor is affected differently from its neighbours.

  153 bold spans across 16 of 16 help files
  prez --help    47 lines showing a literal **
  utilz --help   42
  syncz --help   11

WHAT THE READER SEES. `help/prez.md:57` reads `**`--theme` TAKES A NAME AND NOTHING ELSE...**` and renders as:

  --theme** TAKES A NAME AND NOTHING ELSE (ST0013, hv 29 Aug 2026).** It

The opening `**` and the backticks are consumed, the closing `**` is not. Bold without a leading code span fares no better: `**Version**: run ...` also keeps its asterisks.

WHY IT IS THE RENDERER AND NOT THE SOURCE. Backticks ARE processed -- `PREZ_THEME_PATH` renders unadorned -- while `**` in the same sentence survives. One inline construct is handled and the other is not, in the same pass, so the source is using the documented idiom correctly and the renderer implements half of it.

SEVERITY LOW, DELIBERATELY, AND THE REASON MATTERS MORE THAN THE RATING. Nothing is wrong, missing or misleading: every word of every help file is present and correct, and the only cost is visible punctuation. It is filed rather than fixed because it is estate-wide, in the help pipeline rather than in any utility, and fixing it inside a work package about showreel dispatch would be scope creep into a different subsystem.

NOT RECOMMENDED FOR IMMEDIATE WORK. The honest question is whether anyone is bothered by asterisks in help output, and nobody has said so. If the answer is no, the right close is a deliberate one on the record -- "we accept literal ** in help output" -- rather than leaving it open forever as an implied defect. If the answer is yes, the fix belongs with whoever owns the help pipeline and should handle bold, not add a special case for the pattern that surfaced it.


## CLOSED 2026-09-09 -- THE DEFECT DOES NOT EXIST ON THE PATH USERS USE, AND THE STATED CAUSE IS WRONG

**Both nodes measured through a PIPE, and the figures are an artefact of that.** cc reported 47 / 42 / 11 and vc
reproduced 47 / 42 / 11 EXACTLY. That agreement read as verification and was confirmation of a shared instrument
error.

**MEASURED BY vc, isolating glow itself rather than the help pipeline:**

| invocation                       | literal `**` |
| -------------------------------- | ------------ |
| `glow -s dark   FILE \| cat -v`  | **0**        |
| `glow -s light  FILE \| cat -v`  | **0**        |
| `glow -s auto   FILE \| cat -v`  | **0**        |
| `glow -s notty  FILE \| cat -v`  | **1**        |

**glow selects its `notty` style when stdout is not a terminal, and that style has no bold**, so the markers survive.
Forced to any real style it emits ANSI bold -- `^[[38;5;252;1mbold^[[m`, the `;1m` -- and zero literal `**`. **A user
at a terminal sees bold text and no asterisks.** The asymmetry that made this look like a Utilz bug is glow's own:
inline code has a plain-text representation under `notty` so the backticks go, and bold has none so the markers stay.

**SO THE TITLE AND THE STATED CAUSE MISATTRIBUTE glow's notty STYLESHEET TO UTILZ'S HELP RENDERER.** `show_help` is
not implicated; it calls `glow "$help_file" </dev/null` and glow does the rest. Nothing in `help/*.md` is wrong and
no preprocessing is missing.

**WHAT REMAINS IS REAL AND NOT WORTH ANYTHING**: redirected help output -- `prez --help > file`, a CI log, a pipe into
another tool -- does carry the markers. No such consumer exists in this estate, and a fix would mean overriding a
renderer's own TTY detection to serve a reader nobody has.

**cc reached the right outcome by a weaker route** -- filed low, explicitly not recommended for work, on the grounds
that the cost is visible punctuation nobody is bothered by. The stronger reason is that **there is no visible
punctuation for a user to be bothered by.** Closing on the measurement rather than on the disposition.

**REINSTATE IF** a real consumer of piped help output appears, or if glow's notty stylesheet gains a bold form and
the estate wants it.
